- Transfer mechanism: NimbusCare wants SCCs + addendum. We currently default to SCC-only but can offer EU addendum for enterprise. Is there a material risk to performance/cost?

Subject: Re: NimbusCare DPA redlines + transfer appendix questions — annotated guidance

Rishi / team / Alex — quick counsel notes (see also attached RInfr_privacy_annotated_dpa_v1.docx with inline suggested language):

1) Transfer mechanism (SCCs vs Addendum)
- Recommendation: Offer SCCs by default + an optional Redwood EU Transfer Addendum for enterprise customers that includes the same commitments as the SCCs but with explicit technical and organizational measures. This avoids wholesale reliance on a bespoke transfer mechanism while addressing their ask.
- Suggested language: "Redwood will implement the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module Two), and, upon customer request, execute Redwood's EU Transfer Addendum which supplements the SCCs with additional commitments." (see doc for full text)

2) Subprocessor carve-out
- Position: We cannot accept an open carve-out that permits analytics providers free access to customer data. We can accept a narrow clause: (a) telemetry/analytics subprocessors limited to aggregate/metric data only; (b) prior notice plus 10 business-day objection window for EU-resident subprocessors; (c) contractual flow-down of security obligations.
- Suggested fallback: if NimbusCare insists on a carve-out, accept a defined list of permitted telemetry subprocessors (as schedule) and a monthly notice cadence for updates.

3) Incident notification SLA
- We recommend: Notification of security events affecting customer data within 48 hours of Redwood's detection (initial notification) and a follow-up with a remediation plan within 7 business days. Completely locking to 24 hours is operationally risky and may cause false positives. We can commit to "best-efforts to notify within 24 hours for severe incidents" but need flexibility for triage.

4) Retention and logs
- We can accept a 90-day default retention for request logs with an option for longer retention on customer-specific configuration/policy at additional cost. Strongly push back on unlimited access/escrow-style requests for raw message contents.

5) Execution (DocuSign) and evidence
- We can accommodate DocuSign. Proposed process: Redwood Legal (naomi) will upload Redwood's redline to DocuSign, set signer sequence (NimbusCare legal > Redwood contracting), and include an evidence package (evidence_checklist_RInfr.pdf) listing SOC 2 report availability, architecture diagram, and subprocessor inventory.

Next steps I recommend: Rishi — propose we send a brief annotated summary to Alex (3 bullets: transfers, subprocessors, incident SLA), share the DocuSign envelope link when ready, and request a target for countersign (7 business days). I've attached the annotated doc and a short evidence checklist.

Attachments: RInfr_privacy_annotated_dpa_v1.docx; evidence_checklist_RInfr.pdf

Regards,
Monica Patel
Senior Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference

Monica / Rishi — thanks for the fast turnaround and detailed notes. A few responses from our side (Nina chimed in inline — summarized here):

- Transfer mechanism: Nina says SCCs + addendum is acceptable, provided the addendum is explicit about the limited list of subprocessors and includes a 30-day notice for transfer-related changes. They want the option to require (for regulated data) that certain processing stays in the EU — is that something Redwood's Private deployment can support?
- Subprocessor carve-out: They appreciate the narrow telemetry wording but want the objection window reduced to 5 business days and to include a short list of approved telemetry processors up front.
- Incident SLA: They will accept 48 hours initial notification if we add a clause for "continuous updates every 72 hours" until resolution.

From NimbusCare legal — two additional asks: (a) a one-page appendix that lists evidentiary items (SOC 2 + recent pen test summary) to be attached to the DocuSign envelope; (b) a signature block template for their procurement team so the countersign step is seamless.

We can do a 7-business-day countersign target after receiving your updated redline. If Redwood can confirm Private deployment (eu region) availability and supply the evidence checklist, we'll proceed to countersign.

Best,
Alex Mercer
Head of Legal Operations
NimbusCare

Subject: Re: NimbusCare DPA redlines + annotated privacy comments / execution plan

Alex / Nina — thanks, appreciate the clarity. Quick summary and execution path from Redwood: 

1) Transfers: Redwood will offer SCCs as default and is prepared to provide our Redwood EU Transfer Addendum. For regulated data requiring EU-only processing, Redwood can support Private deployment in EU regions (subject to separate capacity onboarding). I'll have Markus follow up on lead time and costs for Private provisioning.

2) Subprocessors: We will provide an initial permitted telemetry processor list in the schedule and accept your 5 business-day objection window (compromise). Any new EU-resident subprocessor will have 10 business-day notice for review; if the subprocessor touches raw customer content we will not permit without additional agreement.

3) Incident SLA: We'll commit to initial notification within 48 hours and continuous updates every 72 hours until resolved. For "severe" incidents (as defined in the addendum) we'll use best efforts to notify sooner.

4) Evidence & execution: Naomi will upload Redwood's updated redline and an evidence package (SOC 2 summary, pen test high-level) to DocuSign. Proposed signer sequence: NimbusCare (Nina / procurement) -> Redwood Legal (Naomi) -> Redwood Operations (Markus) -> countersign complete. DocuSign envelope will include: updated redline, 1-page evidence appendix, and the signature block template requested.

Next steps / timeline: Naomi will send the DocuSign envelope by tomorrow EOD PST with a 7 business-day review/countersign target. Markus will send a Private deployment lead-time estimate in a separate note. If NimbusCare needs any contract-level exceptions for data residency, please flag them in your countersign notes so we can triage.

If that plan works, I'll mark this thread as "ready for eSign" once Naomi uploads the envelope.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
SVP, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
